data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Resumption must be refused not because of a partial fragment in the log (which is inert), but when and only when the causal fingerprint of the last complete event reveals that an intermediate consumer has already advanced derived state based on a speculative or partial read. The corruption risk lives in downstream state projections, not in the append-only log itself.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If no consumer ever reads partial fragments (all consumers verify framing before processing), this risk vanishes and resumption is always safe given correct framing.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the causal fingerprint does not encode consumer acknowledgments, this mechanism cannot detect the corruption and the claim reduces to the framing-quarantine candidate.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the partial fragment was consumed but the consumer's state is itself discardable (e.g., a cache), divergence is harmless and resumption should proceed.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The append-only log is immutable by definition; a partial fragment cannot corrupt it because it was never granted event identity. The real risk is that some consumer read the partial fragment, interpreted it as a complete event, and updated a state projection. On resumption, the reasoning engine would replay from the last complete event and produce different events, creating a divergence between the log and the already-consumed projection. The causal fingerprint check detects this: if the fingerprint encodes not just the log position but also the set of consumers who have acknowledged reads, a mismatch signals that a partial read was consumed and resumption must be refused.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
